lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Gary, it's Tanya from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the soda swap went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about swimming instead of walking.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So-so. Up and down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the soda swap went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 4.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I can probably manage three days. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the soda swap. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've picked your days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My health is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the soda swap fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, if I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Water just doesn't do it for me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That Coke is part of your routine, and giving it up feels like losing something.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the soda swap going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the parties makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. My grandson thinks it's funny that I have a step counter.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I kept saying tomorrow, tomorrow.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the soda swap going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Let's say I swap soda for water on 5 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 8 and not a 5?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Gary. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Asks about swimming instead of walking; never addressed
Skips swimming question for a yes/no check-in
Commits to three days; motivated by family
Tells client what the goal is really about
Fear of cancer returning motivates change
Wants to feel like herself again
Reflects movement and desire to continue
Feels better when sticking to plan
Names ambivalence about the parties and goal
Repeats earlier question verbatim, ignoring answer at 45-47

flags.reason: Participant asked about swimming instead of walking (line 4); coach moved on without addressing it.
Coach tells Gary what his goal is 'really about' rather than eliciting his meaning; pushes the frame.
Coach repeats line 40 verbatim after Gary answered with procrastination and daughter's help; response was not followed up.
Coach proposes next session time and ignores Gary's request for a later time due to an appointment (line 59).

score.summary: Tanya used good reflections and affirmations, and Gary moved to a concrete goal of five water swaps with an 8/10 confidence and a rain plan. However, she skipped his swimming question, repeated an earlier question verbatim, and did not settle the next contact time when Gary asked for a later slot.
strengths: Reflected ambivalence well at line 42 ('On one hand... On the other hand...').
Elicited and reinforced change talk, e.g. line 10 and line 26 reflections, and line 54 asking why he chose an 8.
Built a concrete plan with confidence rating and barrier planning (lines 51-57).
coaching_tips: Answer or defer Gary's swimming question at line 4 before moving on; it was a direct request for information.
Replace the repeated question at line 48 with a reflection of his answer at line 47 (e.g., 'Tomorrow keeps creeping in, and your daughter helps only sometimes').
At line 12, ask what the goal means to him instead of stating it; for example, 'What would getting your life back look like?'
Confirm or reschedule the next call at line 59 before closing, and summarize the goal and barrier plan first.
